hardening_shipped: a durable identity write is removed from a GET: opening Settings → Activation on an unminted install no longer creates the install's correlation id (the get_or_create_*-on-a-read class, ledger 2026-08-05; third occurrence after #1987 and the ent#190 benchmark read)

the mint is a write-once claim decided by the PRIMARY KEY, so two workers that SELECT-miss together land one id and the loser reads the winner's back — the last-write-wins race #1987 recorded as pre-existing (orphaning one worker's product_events rows) is closed

the enterprise suite's never-mint proof sits on the write SINK (database.db.set_setting / insert_setting_if_absent raise) plus a static AST guard over the service module, so neither a re-added top-level import nor a lazy in-function import can mint without failing CI
the footer never claims 'not minted' for a value that is merely absent or malformed: only the backend's explicit null renders that state; an admin sees 'unavailable' otherwise
no new log line, no new outbound call, no new setting: the id is not logged by the new code; the funnel stays local-only
